title: Run a renderer and email its stdout
summary: Execute one manifest job and send successful nonempty stdout unchanged as plain-text email to the fixed personal recipient.
use_when: Execute a configured collection-and-render script and email its successful stdout, or inspect its manifest and supported output contract.
do_not_use_when: The request needs a saved-message preview, report-history read, retry of a retained payload, another recipient, source-specific reporting, or delivery confirmation.
outcome: One renderer execution either skips empty successful stdout or returns Email submission acceptance for the exact nonempty plain-text output.
effects: Execution starts a trusted normal-user renderer; successful nonempty stdout is disclosed through Email. Paperboy retains no rendered body or structured send ledger. Scheduled logs can retain result metadata. Scripts own any source reads and side effects.
authority: Paperboy validates execution and stdout; renderers own data and report meaning. Email owns submission acceptance; Gmail owns final delivery. Clockwork owns scheduled runtime evidence.
success: Renderer exit success and zero stdout bytes establish a skip. Otherwise a successful Email receipt establishes Resend submission acceptance for the unchanged stdout body, not inbox delivery or source completeness.
failure_and_recovery: Nonzero renderer exit, timeout, invalid UTF-8, or oversized stdout sends no email. Stderr stays separate and diagnostics exclude captured stdout. No saved body or structured retry state remains.
Email timeout or interruption can leave acceptance unknown. Inspect Resend before a new run when duplication matters. A new run renders again; it cannot resume or reconcile the prior payload.

Scheduled failures use Clockwork halt-until-approved with its shared service-health delay. Later activations can occur while failure is pending. Exact incident approval permits future admission and does not retry failed work.
privacy: Scripts run with current-user access. Captured stdout stays in memory for Email handoff and is not printed or logged by Paperboy. Script stderr may contain private data in bounded diagnostics. Email loads credentials and discloses subject and body to Resend and Gmail.
does_not_authorize: Discovery does not authorize executing a script, sending email, enabling a schedule, or treating uncertain acceptance as confirmed nonacceptance.

consumers.statement: The current user and explicitly authorized installed scheduled Paperboy jobs.

preconditions.statement: A valid selected version-one TOML manifest, readable executable renderer, supported Email wrapper, and authority for script execution and its resulting personal email. Scheduled execution also requires an applied enabled Clockwork binding.

inputs.statement: An absolute manifest selection or the default Paperboy manifest and one stable job ID. Each job supplies nonempty render argv with an absolute executable, an optional subject defaulting to its ID, and one supported interval or local-calendar schedule. Literal -c arguments are unsupported. The selected regular UTF-8 manifest is at most 1 MiB and rejects unknown fields. Arguments contain no NUL; explicit subjects are nonblank and contain no control characters.

outputs.statement: Results return job_id, body_bytes, and outcome skipped_empty or accepted; accepted results add provider_message_id. Default output is formatted JSON; --json selects compact ok/data or stderr ok:false/error envelopes. No captured stdout appears in the result. status-snapshot uses raw Iatreion schema one.

data_semantics.statement: Successful nonempty stdout is the unchanged plain-text body; stderr is separate. Zero bytes skip Email, while whitespace-only output is sent. Scripts own collection semantics and reporting windows; Paperboy retains no body or occurrence ledger.

identity_and_units.statement: Job IDs are at most 63 ASCII bytes, begin with a lowercase letter, and continue with lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens. Each maps to paperboy/JOB_ID. Interval values are whole seconds; calendar values are local hour and minute; output limits count bytes. There is no durable per-run message identity.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: List reads configured jobs, not history. Manual execution selects current manifest configuration; scheduled execution selects an applied immutable command snapshot. Neither freezes renderer file bytes or data.
Source accuracy, completeness, freshness, start delay, throughput, and inbox arrival time are not promised.

access.statement: Literal command execution uses the executable parent as cwd and clears ambient environment except HOME, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:HOME/.local/bin, and CHANCERY_USAGE_INTERNAL=1. Scripts run as the current user under operating-system permissions, without a Paperboy sandbox. Renderer stdin is closed.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Paperboy waits for successful renderer exit before invoking Email once. It retains no payload or structured send ledger and performs no process retry. Scheduled logs can retain execution results including receipt IDs, but supply no replay interface. Applied schedules fix argv, subject, and absolute Email wrapper path without runtime manifest reads. Separate executions render again and do not reuse a prior message identity.

operational_limits.statement: Manifest maximum 1 MiB; renderer timeout 1200 seconds; stdout maximum 64000 UTF-8 bytes, rejected rather than truncated; stderr diagnostic prefix 4096 bytes, excess drained and discarded; Email observation 120 seconds; Clockwork timeout 1380 seconds. Interval range 1 through 31536000; local hour 0 through 23 and minute 0 through 59; run-at-load false.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: TOML version one is the configuration format. Paperboy exposes literal renderer execution and stdout submission without retained payloads or a send-recovery interface.
No general future compatibility or deprecation window is promised.

reliances.statement: Email supplies fixed personal-recipient submission, bounded within-invocation transport retries, and provider-acceptance receipts.
Clockwork supplies immutable activation definitions, binding selection, overlap control, runtime history, delayed failure halts, incidents, and exact continuation approval.
